newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EMI's Lamfalussy says supports EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: EMI's Lamfalussy says supports EMU stability pact.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) president Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Monday that he supported the idea of a stability pact to ensure fiscal rigour under monetary union but declined to speculate on whether the agreement could be amended.

"I don't want to take part in the discussion about the stability pact .. I don't want to comment on the specifics," Lamfalussy told reporters on the fringes of the annual meeting of the Bank of International Settlements.
Lamfalussy said the EMI, the forerunner of the European Central Bank, was largely in favour of a strong stability pact but that it was not responsible for hammering out the details.
"I have always expressed support for a strong stability pact," Lamfalussy said, adding however that it was up to the governments to decide the specifics.
There has been speculation that the French might seek a renegotiation of the stability pact during the Amsterdam summit meeting of EU leaders on June 16 and 17.
The pact has already been agreed in principle.
